subject: SOC 2 re-attestation: evidence routing playbook + burst capacity amendment
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Owens <lisa.owens@starlite.com>, Michael Jansen <michael.jansen@starlite.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 re-attestation: evidence routing playbook + burst capacity amendment

Hi Lisa / Michael —

Thanks again for the quick call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a short operational playbook and a proposed amendment to the renewal that covers two things Starlite requested: (1) a documented evidence routing process for SOC 2 re-attestation and (2) short-term burst capacity during the audit window.

Key asks from your side we captured:
- Confirm retention horizon for audit logs (current prod: 365 days). You mentioned legal is evaluating 540 days as an internal policy.
- Confirm whether Starlite requires an on-prem evidence escrow or if secure Drive handoff is sufficient.
- Procurement asked for a one-time credit to offset staging transfer costs; I noted that with Ben.

Attachments included: evidence matrix (starlite_evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a short PDF with the retention amendment language (redwood_retention_proposal.pdf). I also linked a draft ops playbook in the Drive.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) You confirm retention horizon preference by 2026-10-05.
2) We finalize the amendment language and include it as an addendum to the renewal (we can ship a DocuSign link after legal confirms).
3) If you need audit-time burst capacity, tell us which 14-day window you want us to reserve so we can size Dedicated pools and price accordingly.

If helpful, Kimberly can provide a short note on how log retention impacts our hosting regions and implications for data residency. Ben is on pricing if procurement wants a one-off credit to assist the migration.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.com
+1 415-555-9142

From: Lisa Owens <lisa.owens@starlite.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Jansen <michael.jansen@starlite.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation: evidence routing playbook + burst capacity amendment

Tessa —

Appreciate the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our security team after reviewing your matrix: 

1) Retention: Legal prefers 540 days for audit logs (EU-regulated workloads). Can Redwood support a 540-day retention for our account while keeping other customers at 365? If there are material cost implications we need to see a delta.
2) Evidence handoff: Secure Drive handoff is acceptable provided logs are hashed and we get an MD5/SHA256 manifest. We will not require an on-prem escrow for this engagement unless we hit the forensic stage.
3) Burst capacity: We expect audit activity in January 2027. At present we are planning a 21-day window starting 2027-01-10.
4) Procurement: I looped in procurement@starlite.com — they will follow up on credit language.

Please confirm whether the 540-day retention is a configuration-only change or requires a contract addendum and any pricing delta for dedicated storage. Also confirm whether the January window can be booked now and whether Redwood recommends a particular sizing multiplier for the burst (we're currently on a 4-GPU Dedicated pool).

Thanks,
Lisa Owens
Head of Security Operations
Starlite Financial
lisa.owens@starlite.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Owens <lisa.owens@starlite.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation: evidence routing playbook + burst capacity amendment

Lisa —

Short answers up front: yes, we can support 540 days for a single customer (account-level retention override); we'll document it as a contract addendum to the renewal because it changes the default data horizon and has storage/cost implications. Pricing delta depends on two factors: additional storage for retained log volumes and the extra snapshot/backup schedule during the retention window.

On burst sizing: for a 4-GPU Dedicated pool currently supporting your baseline, we recommend reserving a 2x multiplier (so book 8 GPUs) for the 21-day window to keep tail-latency low during parallel evidence exports and snapshotting. We can hold that capacity as a provisional reservation now and finalize sizing 60 days before the window.

Operational controls we will implement (ops playbook highlights):
- Evidence routing: explicit Drive destinations with manifest generation (SHA256) + automated transfer jobs.
- Audit window: automatic prefix caching disabled during heavy snapshot exports to avoid cache eviction during the snapshot run and minimize token double-counting.
- Retention addendum: will explicitly state 540-day retention for Starlite-only, list affected systems, and include rollback steps.

Ben will propose a one-time staging credit and Kimberly will draft a short legal-friendly amendment. I placed the ops playbook draft in the Drive link and attached an initial redwood_retention_proposal.pdf.

—Tessa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SOC 2 re-attestation: evidence routing playbook + burst capacity amendment

Tessa / Kimberly —

I reviewed the proposed addendum impact and put together two quick options for procurement to consider: 

Option A (config + small storage uplift): 540-day retention implemented as an account-level config. Estimated incremental storage cost: ~€1,200/month (based on current ingest and retention curves). One-time staging support credit: €4,000.
Option B (contracted reserved storage + SLA): Addendum includes reserved storage commitment and premium snapshot retention (24/7 retention replication across two EU regions). Incremental cost: ~€2,800/month, one-time staging credit: €2,000, and a 6% discount on the reserved capacity line for the annual renewal.

For the January burst window (21 days) we can provision an 8-GPU reservation as Tessa suggested. Preliminary hold price (provisional, refundable up to 60 days prior): €18,500 for the 21-day hold. If procurement prefers to bake the burst into the renewal pricing we can offer a reduced rate; happy to convert those numbers into a compact amendment for procurement@starlite.com.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Michael Jansen <michael.jansen@starlite.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Lisa Owens <lisa.owens@starlite.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@starlite.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation: evidence routing playbook + burst capacity amendment

Tessa / Ben / Kimberly —

Thanks for the clarity. Procurement prefers Option B because our internal auditors want the replication SLA called out. Please go ahead and draft the addendum language and a DocuSign package; we will aim to get signatures by 2026-11-03.

Action items we have on our side:
- Procurement will review the exact numbers and come back with any redlines (expect by 2026-10-08).
- Security will confirm manifest/hash formatting (we will provide a sample SHA256 manifest format by next Wed).
- We request Redwood place a provisional hold for the 8-GPU burst window (2027-01-10 through 2027-01-30) and we will finalize sizing once procurement completes.

Appreciate the responsiveness — this looks straightforward.

—Michael
Michael Jansen
VP, Technology Risk & Controls
